entries.why: Source says the RAP was 'approved by the Bank' and the Panel 'is not aware that any such payment has been made'; 'tied to them' and 'found no record' were not in the source.
Quoted phrase 'in compliance with the requirements of the World Bank' does not appear; source says 'to comply more closely with present requirements of the World Bank'.
Replaced paraphrase with the report's own words; the report does not say 'Bank clearance' or call it a loan condition.

Removed the government cash payments to the Ministry of Transmigration: the source says the government made these 'as it did for all others', not as a term of the loan. Added the source's 'successive revisions in the loan agreement'. No 'required' wording used; source does not say the loan was conditional on the 1989 program.

Terms confirmed in the Himachal Pradesh Agreement dated May 18, 1989 (Sections 2.02, 2.06, 4.02, Schedule). Changed 'law' to 'safeguard': applying for forest clearance under an existing law is an environmental permit step, not a change of law.

Source says compensation was 'scheduled to be paid prior to the impoundment' and the Bank 'will require NELSAP to open escrow accounts'; moved the tag reason from a budget allocation to that stated requirement.
Confirmed. Source calls the action plan the October 2008 ESAP; it does not say it was 'attached to the loan'.
Matched source wording ('enter into an agreement with a reputable NGO or other acceptable party'); added that contracts were issued April 2005, after the October 2004 Kilwa events.
Press release opened with WebFetch: it says 'signed', and lists no formal loan conditions. Added a plain statement that neither source calls these conditions.

The Social and Labour Plan was a legal condition of Lonmin's South African mining rights, not of IFC's loan. The CAO says the loan covenant covered the Performance Standards and the EMPRs, which included an SLP commitment; reworded accordingly.
The only 'term' was an outcome of the CAO mediation, not a condition attached to IFC's money.

Source does not say 'required'; it says the plans were prepared 'accordingly' after the Category A ratings. Removed the Safeguard Policy Statement link, which the source makes only in ADB Management's response.
The plan does include Performance Requirement 5 actions (temporary restricted access to land), so 'did not address resettlement' was removed; confirmed no mention of landslides or geohazards.
Confirmed amounts, date and the list of applicable standards (ESCM, October 25, 2006). Text says 'listed ... as applying', not 'required', which matches the source.

ICIJ does state an ADB condition, but does not say which loan, when, or that it was tied to the concession; 'law' also did not fit a water-loss target. IFC was an adviser, not lending, and the World Bank/ADB 'pushed' for privatization, which is pressure, not a stated condition. Text kept as reporting, tag removed.

Confirmed by WebFetch; aligned wording with the source ('annual deficit targets', 'fifth review ... not completed'). Kept 'cuts' tag on the deficit targets, but note the source names deficit targets, not spending cuts as such.
Confirmed ('8% required by 1974 under the Loan Agreement'). Source says costs were shared 50/50 between lenders and Ghana and extra resettlement was a 'non-project item'; reworded those two points.
Source has a firmer term than the original text: the ESCP made activities in the four protected areas wait for the VMGPs. Tag now rests on that.
Confirmed in the Portuguese report: $130m IDA within $210m, NAS5 applicable, cut-off 13 December 2023, PIU statement and requesters' demolition claims. Text does not say 'required'.
Confirmed by WebFetch (PR 1.9, PR 5.39, para. 40). The report did not tie herders directly to PR 5 compensation in the part read, so 'including herders' was split out.
The audit does not name PT Asiatic Persada, and the tag rested on what the Performance Standards 'expect', not on a stated loan condition.
The land tag rested on a note about the Government's delay in securing land, which is not a condition. The document is a Project Completion Report Validation, not an 'Interim Evaluation'.
Source says 'conditions on the Bank's credit called for' the plan; made that explicit and added the March 1982 deadline.
Source presents these as items in an 'agreed' ESAP closing gaps with IFC's requirements, worded 'the company will'; replaced 'required'. Amounts are what IFC was 'considering'.
Confirmed standard E&S conditions for all disbursements and that ESAP items were left out of the agreement; source says 'first disbursement' in April 2009.
Confirmed: Loan 3632-IN, EAP and two RAPs, OD 4.30 'borrower is required to prepare a resettlement action plan acceptable to the Bank', land-for-land or cash options.

Confirmed: 'contingent on timely and effective implementation' (Management to NGOs, May 1996, cross-conditionality); Parej East IPDP not reviewed. Text already attributes it to what Management told NGOs.
Confirmed: PAD says all transmission sub-projects 'will require an environmental assessment'; 1999 Framework 'required all sub-projects to prepare' an EMP and RAP.
Confirmed in Project Agreement dated January 22, 2010, Schedule Sections D-H.
Confirmed: Diamondbank manages the facility; 'Shell's lead in allowing its contracts to be used as security for credit'.
Confirmed amounts, 1993 loan agreement (1988 OHS guidelines), 1999 agreement (Pollution Prevention and Abatement Handbook, IFC EHS Guidelines), no E&S terms in equity agreement, loans repaid 2005.

Confirmed by WebFetch: plans 'required by the IFC', hazardous materials/emergency plans 'supposed to have been completed before the first loan disbursement', tailings plan due six months before filling. (IFC later let those plans be finished before operations began.)
Confirmed: SDR 46.0M (US$68.5M), Financing Agreement May 7, 2007, IPPF 'became an obligation of the borrower under the legal agreements', no RAP for any forest area.
Confirmed by WebFetch on both IMF pages; MEFP dated December 8, 2000 does not label the NFRA or ADMARC items as performance criteria.
Confirmed: IDA guarantee approved April 26, 2007, ~US$360m WBG support, legal agreements to require an EPRP, Kalagala offset in the Indemnity Agreement.
Confirmed by WebFetch: Agreement of 2 May 1968, Sections 7.01(b)-(c), 5.01, 2.05.
Confirmed in Hansard 31 July 1956: loan service guaranteed by the UK and up to £10m of its sterling subscription used.

Confirmed in Loan Agreement and Project Agreement dated January 15, 2008 (RAP/SCDP, no construction before compensation and relocation, EMP, debt/equity 4:1, receivables 3 months, Himachal Pradesh duties).
Confirmed: suspension effective April 18, 2024 quote; Second Request statement on RAPs.
Confirmed: September 2022 $200m, 2,775 PAPs, compensation 'needed before the earthworks and bus depot construction can begin', agreed action on ESS 5.
Confirmed: SDR 16.9m (~US$25m), approved February 24, 2004, second-phase trigger, DCA covenant on lands adjacent to Ethnic Lands, no remedies for Property Law effects.
